rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The effects of obedience and disobedience return to the human being, who is poor and dependent on God.
rows.anchor: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها الإسراء 7

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting produces taqwa by training a person to restrain bodily pleasures and worldly attachments in pursuit of spiritual purity and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: فإن كل إنسان يشعر بفطرته أن من أراد الاتصال بعالم الطهارة والرفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For ordinary people, abstaining from permitted food, drink, and intercourse trains the will to avoid sins; obedience in permitted desires prepares greater obedience in prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وأقرب من ذلك وأمس لحال عموم الناس من أهل الدنيا وأهل الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative أيامًا معدودات is adverbial with an understood في and is governed by الصيام.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الظرفية بتقدير، في، ومتعلق بقوله الصيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite days described as counted make the burden seem small and encourage the person obligated to fast.
rows.anchor: تنكير أيام واتصافه بالعدد للدلالة على تحقير التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ramadan clause explains the counted days: the prescribed counted period is the month of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالأيام المعدودات شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the counted days as three days of fasting each month plus the fast of Ashura, later superseded by the Ramadan command.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين أن المراد بالأيام المعدودات ثلاث أيام من كل شهر وصوم يوم عاشوراء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported view specifies the three monthly fasts as the white days and adds Ashura; Muhammad and Muslims supposedly fasted these until Ramadan replaced the rule.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم والثلاث الأيام هي الأيام البيض من كل شهر وصوم يوم عاشوراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects this chronology: a universal, public act of worship would have a settled historical record, yet its occurrence and abrogation are disputed.
rows.anchor: الصيام كما قيل عبادة عامة شاملة، ولو كان الأمر كما يقولون لضبطه التاريخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the Umayyads fabricated Ashura's status as a fast and festival after Karbala, inventing reports of ancient and broadly Islamic celebration despite no historical or religious basis.
rows.anchor: مما ابتدعه بنو أمية لعنهم الله حيث أبادوا فيه ذرية رسول الله وأهل بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax makes the Ramadan statement explain the counted days, so the three verses form one coherent passage prescribing the Ramadan fast.
rows.anchor: فيكون بيانا للأيام المعدودات ويكون جميع الآيات الثلث كلاما واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if Ramadan is read as an independent subject with its own predicate, it does not contradict the preceding verse and therefore cannot abrogate it.
rows.anchor: غير أنها لا تصلح حينئذ لأن تكون ناسخة لما قبلها لعدم المنافات بينها وبين سابقتها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says Christians' fast grew to fifty days after Jesus, Muslims received that fast under the first command, and the counted-days verse later replaced it.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الصوم كان مكتوبا على النصارى ثم زادوا فيه ونقصوا بعد عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls that abrogation account weaker and more plainly false: the counted-days clause continues the first command, and its supporting reports conflict with Quranic wording and context.
rows.anchor: وكون الآية الثانية من متممات الآية الأولى أظهر وأجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء marks a consequence: the illness-or-travel ruling follows from the prior prescription of fasting.
rows.anchor: الفاء للتفريع والجملة متفرعة على قوله كتب عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fast is obligatory and its number is integral to the obligation; illness or travel requires an equal number of make-up days outside Ramadan, completing the missed count.
rows.anchor: لا يرفع اليد عن العدد، فلو عرض عارض يوجب ارتفاع الحكم الفرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مرض is the opposite of health; سفر derives from disclosure or uncovering, as travel exposes someone beyond the home where they reside.
rows.anchor: المرض خلاف الصحة والسفر مأخوذ من السفر بمعنى الكشف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying one is on a journey rather than calling one a traveler indicates present involvement in the state, excluding past or future travel.
rows.anchor: للإشارة إلى اعتبار فعلية التلبس حالا دون الماضي والمستقبل

rows.speaker: المعظم من علماء أهل السنة والجماعة
rows.claim: Most Sunni scholars, along with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf, ʿUmar, Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Hurayra, and ʿUrwa, read illness or travel as a concession to fast or break the fast.
rows.anchor: وهم المعظم من علماء أهل السنة والجماعة - إن المدلول عليه بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i prefers the Ahl al-Bayt Imams' reported view that an ill or traveling person must break the Ramadan fast and make up the same number of days.
rows.anchor: وهو المروي عن أئمة أهل البيت، وهو مذهب جمع من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The optional-fast view supplies an unstated فأفطر after the travel clause, an ellipsis contrary to the apparent wording and unsupported by any contextual clue.
rows.anchor: فقالوا إن التقدير فمن كان مريضا أو على سفر فأفطر فعدة من أيام أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even with that ellipsis, saying a person who broke the fast owes make-up days only shows broad permissibility, not an optional concession; the legislative context and omitted duty weigh against that reading.
rows.anchor: وأما كونه جائزا بمعنى عدم كونه إلزاميا فلا دليل عليه من الكلام البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some define إطاقة as spending one's full capacity on an act, which entails exertion and hardship.
rows.anchor: الإطاقة كما ذكره بعضهم صرف تمام الطاقة في الفعل، ولازمه وقوع الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fidya is a substitute, here a financial substitute: enough ordinary food to satisfy one hungry poor person.
rows.anchor: والفدية هي البدل وهي هنا بدل مالي وهو طعام مسكين أي طعام يشبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fidya obligation is mandatory, like make-up fasting for illness or travel; وعلى الذين indicates assignment rather than an optional concession.
rows.anchor: وحكم الفدية أيضا فرض كحكم القضاء في المريض والمسافر لمكان قوله وعلى الذين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say early Muslims unused to fasting could choose between fasting and feeding a poor person daily; Ramadan later abrogated this for the capable, while the elderly, pregnant, and nursing retained fidya.
rows.anchor: أن الجملة تفيد الرخصة ثم نسخت، فهو سبحانه وتعالى خير المطيقين للصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That reading disrupts the unified passage: it first prescribes fasting, then lets able people replace it with fidya, then commands everyone present for Ramadan to fast.
rows.anchor: فتارة يقول كتب عليكم الصيام، وأخرى يقول يجوز على القادرين منكم الإفطار والفدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abrogation scheme lacks a basis for making يطيقونه mean ability before abrogation but inability afterward, and a universal later command cannot selectively preserve a rule supposedly limited to the unable.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يقال إن قوله يطيقون، كان دالا على القدرة قبل النسخ فصار يدل بعد النسخ على عدم القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the compounded abrogation scheme in which Ramadan replaces counted days and counted days in turn replace the initial fasting command; adding these stages makes the reading absurd.
rows.anchor: ما ذكروه من نسخ قوله { شهر رمضان } إلخ لقوله { أياما معدودات } إلخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تطوع is formed on the تفعّل pattern from طوع, willingness as opposed to compulsion; it means undertaking an act willingly, without reluctance.
rows.anchor: التطوع تفعل من الطوع مقابل الكره وهو إتيان الفعل بالرضا والرغبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word's form and root do not restrict it to recommended acts; Muslim usage narrowed it to supererogation later because obligation was associated with compulsion.
rows.anchor: لا دلالة فيه مادة وهيئة على الندب وعلى هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause follows from the passage's account of fasting as beneficial, good, and eased for the community: perform the prescribed fast willingly, since willing good is better than reluctant good.
rows.anchor: الصوم مكتوب عليكم مرعيا فيه خيركم وصلاحكم مع ما فيه من استقراركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse puts the cause, willingly doing any good is good, in place of its result, willingly undertaking the fast is good; he compares this ellipsis to 6:33.
rows.anchor: من قبيل وضع السبب موضع المسبب، أعني وضع كون التطوع بمطلق الخير خيرا

rows.speaker: ربما يقال
rows.claim: An alternative connects the clause to fidya: anyone who voluntarily gives more than one poor person's food, such as double, does better.
rows.anchor: وربما يقال إن الجملة أعني قوله تعالى { فمن تطوع خيرا فهو خير له } ، مرتبطة بالجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the extra-fidya reading: تطوع is not shown to mean recommended giving, the causal link is obscure, and doing good voluntarily is not the same as increasing a payment.
rows.anchor: فأنه لا يظهر لتفرع التطوع بالزيادة على حكم الفدية وجه معقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This completes the previous thought: willingly fast the prescribed fast, since willing good is good and fasting benefits you, making willing fasting good upon good.
rows.anchor: تطوعوا بالصوم المكتوب عليكم فإن التطوع بالخير خير والصوم خير لكم

rows.speaker: ربما يقال
rows.claim: A proposed reading addresses excused people and recommends that ill or traveling people choose fasting over breaking the fast and making it up; al-Tabataba'i rejects this.
rows.anchor: يحمل على رجحان الصوم واستحبابه على أصحاب الرخصة من المريض والمسافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed audience shift lacks evidence, and the preceding clause is third person while this one directly addresses its audience, weakening the claimed continuity as advice to the excused.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الجملتين أعني قوله { فمن كان منكم } إلخ، وقوله { وأن تصوموا خير لكم } ، بالغيبة والخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal treats the first clause as a choice, yet فعدة من أيام أخر indicates that make-up fasting is prescribed, not simply optional.
rows.anchor: بل ظاهر قوله { فعدة من أيام أخر } ، تعين الصوم في أيام أخر كما مر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior clause names Ramadan fasting and later make-up days, not a choice between fasting and breaking; nothing signals a comparison favoring Ramadan fasting over make-up days.
rows.anchor: لا سبيل إلى استفاده ترجيح صوم شهر رمضان على صوم غيره من مجرد قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage explains the rationale of legislation, not the legal ruling itself, so calling an act خير لكم does not make its ruling non-obligatory.
rows.anchor: وأن المقام ليس مقام بيان الحكم حتى ينافي ظهور الرجحان كون الحكم وجوبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legislated command necessarily contains benefit, goodness, and virtue; this rationale is compatible with obligation.
rows.anchor: وأن الحكم المشرع لا يخلو عن المصلحة والخير والحسن كما في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan is the ninth Arabian lunar month, between Sha'ban and Shawwal, and it is the only month named in the Quran.
rows.anchor: شهر رمضان هو الشهر التاسع من الشهور القمرية العربية بين شعبان وشوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نزول is arrival at a destination from above; إنزال denotes descent all at once, whereas تنزيل denotes gradual descent.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الإنزال والتنزيل، أن الإنزال دفعي والتنزيل تدريجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran names the book revealed to Muhammad in its capacity as recited; it denotes either the entire book or portions of it.
rows.anchor: والقرآن اسم للكتاب المنزل على نبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم باعتبار كونه مقروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ramadan statement appears to conflict with 17:106 and the widely transmitted history that the Quran descended gradually across the roughly twenty-three-year prophetic mission.
rows.anchor: وهو ظاهر في نزوله تدريجيا في مجموع مدة الدعوة وهي ثلاث وعشرون سنة تقريبا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One proposed reconciliation says the entire Quran descended to the lowest heaven in Ramadan, then came to the Prophet in portions over the mission's twenty-three years; the author says this answer comes from reports.
rows.anchor: أنه نزل دفعة على سماء الدنيا في شهر رمضان ثم نزل على رسول الله

words: هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An objection to the lowest-heaven account says the following description as guidance and discriminator does not fit a book remaining in heaven for years.
rows.anchor: لا يساعد على ذلك إذ لا معنى لبقائه على وصف الهداية والفرقان في السماء مدة سنين

words: هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The reply says guidance and discrimination may be present as a capacity before their effects occur, like statutory provisions that take effect when their time arrives.
rows.anchor: وفارقا أذا التبس حق بباطل لا ينافي بقائه مدة على حال الشأنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the analogy: statutes differ from speech addressed to an audience, which cannot precede its moment of address even briefly.
rows.anchor: أن حكم القوانين والدساتير غير حكم الخطابات التي لا يستقيم أن تتقدم على مقام التخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites commands to repent and sacrifice oneself, hasten to Friday prayer, and believe and strive as خير لكم, showing that benefit language can accompany obligatory commands.
rows.anchor: والآيات في ذلك كثيرة خامسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic speech can address events as they occur, as in the verses about a woman's plea, people leaving for trade, and believers fulfilling their covenant.
rows.anchor: قد سمع الله قول التي تجادلك في زوجها وتشتكي إلى الله والله يسمع تحاوركما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran contains abrogating and abrogated rulings, which cannot coexist at the same time in the sequence of revelation.
rows.anchor: على أن في القرآن ناسخا ومنسوخا، ولا معنى لاجتماعهما في زمان بحسب النزول

rows.speaker: ربما أجيب
rows.claim: Another proposed answer takes the Ramadan descent to mean only the first portion revealed, but he rejects it as unsupported and historically implausible.
rows.anchor: وربما أجيب عن الإشكال أن المراد من نزول القرآن في شهر رمضان أن أول ما نزل منه نزل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual account places Muhammad's commissioning on 27 Rajab, more than thirty days before Ramadan; the first verses of al-ʿAlaq and al-Muddaththir also locate revelation at the mission's start.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إنما بعث بالقرآن، وقد بعث اليوم السابع والعشرين من شهر رجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is highly unlikely that the first revelation waited until Ramadan; neither this verse nor the similar blessed-night and Laylat al-Qadr verses say only the first portion descended then.
rows.anchor: على أن قوله تعالى { أنزل فيه القرآن } ، غير صريح الدلالة على أن المراد بالقرآن أول نازل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ramadan and sacred-night verses use إنزال, signaling a single descent, unlike تنزيل for the Quran's gradual revelation.
rows.anchor: عبرت عن ذلك بلفظ الإنزال الدال على الدفعة دون التنزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He applies this single-descent wording to the parallel blessed-night and Laylat al-Qadr statements as well as the Ramadan verse.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى حم * والكتاب المبين إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He introduces a different account of the Ramadan descent, saying close consideration of Quranic passages points beyond the proposed lowest-heaven and first-portion explanations.
rows.anchor: والذي يعطيه التدبر في آيات الكتاب أمر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's visible detail is secondary to a prior, undivided book: 11:1 says its verses were first made firm and only then set out in detail.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا الإحكام مقابل التفصيل، والتفصيل هو جعله فصلا فصلا وقطعة قطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From 7:52–53 and 10:37–39, he infers that detailed form overlays the original book; deniers fail to know its ta'wil, which they will confront at judgment, and the original is that detailed Quran's ta'wil.
rows.anchor: فإن الآيات الشريفة وخاصة ما في سورة يونس ظاهرة الدلالة على أن التفصيل أمر طار على الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zukhruf 43:1–4 describes an Arabic, recited form made for human understanding, while the original remains in God's elevated and undivided Umm al-Kitab.
rows.anchor: إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran has a hidden location in the guarded book, touched only by the purified; before its descent it remains concealed from outsiders.
rows.anchor: إنه لقرآن كريم في كتاب مكنون لا يمسه إلا المطهرون تنزيل من رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This concealed book is called Umm al-Kitab in Zukhruf and the Preserved Tablet in al-Buruj, preserved from alteration.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي عبر عنه في آيات الزخرف، بأم الكتاب، وفي سورة البروج، باللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the gradual revealed Quran includes abrogation and change over time, the Clear Book that is its source is a reality beyond the revealed form, which is like its garment.
rows.anchor: فالكتاب المبين الذي هو أصل القرآن وحكمه الخالي عن التفصيل أمر وراء هذا المنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes the revealed Quran as garment, image, and likeness of the underlying reality; this relation permits Quran to name the source itself, as in 85:21.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة اللباس من المتلبس وبمنزلة المثال من الحقيقة وبمنزلة المثل من الغرض المقصود بالكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus the Ramadan and sacred-night descent refers to the underlying Reality of the Book descending to Muhammad's heart all at once, while its detailed Quranic form descends gradually during his mission.
rows.anchor: على إنزال حقيقة الكتاب والكتاب المبين إلى قلب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم دفعة
